name: Othniel and Achsah
charge: Taking Kirjath-sepher at Caleb's word; and asking for the springs as well as the land
summary: Caleb offered his daughter to whoever would smite Kirjath-sepher and take it. His younger brother's son Othniel took it and was given her. As she came to him she moved him to ask her father for a field, and lighted off her ass, and Caleb said, What wouldest thou? She asked for a blessing: thou hast given me a south land, give me also springs of water. He gave her the upper springs and the nether springs. Othniel became the first judge of Israel.
offense: Two obediences, one of arms and one of speech. Othniel took a fortified city on the strength of a word rather than a strategy (Joshua 15:17). Achsah's is the more instructive: she had been given a portion in the dry south (Joshua 15:19), which was a lawful gift and an insufficient one, and rather than resent it she got down off the ass and asked, framing the request as a blessing rather than a complaint, thou hast given me a south land, give me also springs of water. She asked the right person, at the right moment, for the thing the land actually needed.
judgment: He gave her the upper springs and the nether springs (Joshua 15:19), which is more than she asked for, and the detail is repeated in Joshua and in Judges so that the record carries it twice (Joshua 15:16-19). Othniel afterwards had the Spirit of the Lord come upon him (Judges 3:9), judged Israel, went out to war, and the land had rest forty years (Judges 3:11). The first deliverer in the book of Judges came out of a household in (Judges 1:1) which a daughter asked well and a father gave more than was requested (Joshua 15:13).

verses.text: And Caleb said, He that smiteth Kirjath–sepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife.
And Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to wife.
And it came to pass, as she came unto him, that she moved him to ask of her father a field: and she lighted off her ass; and Caleb said unto her, What wouldest thou?
Who answered, Give me a blessing; for thou hast given me a south land; give me also springs of water. And he gave her the upper springs, and the nether springs.
And Caleb said, He that smiteth Kirjath–sepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife.
And Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to wife.
And it came to pass, when she came to him, that she moved him to ask of her father a field: and she lighted from off her ass; and Caleb said unto her, What wilt thou?
And she said unto him, Give me a blessing: for thou hast given me a south land; give me also springs of water. And Caleb gave her the upper springs and the nether springs.

entries.commentary: This is the lot of the tribe of the children of Judah by their families, even to the border of Edom: the south border ran from the shore of the salt sea, up the south side of Kadeshbarnea, and out unto the river of Egypt, with the goings out of that coast at the sea. We are not locating every one of these places as we read, but as you go back and listen, look these places up in your Bible atlas so you can see the actual areas being read about in the region.

The east border was the salt sea unto the end of Jordan; the north border went up from the bay of the sea, by Bethhogla and the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben, and up by the valley of the son of Hinnom unto the south side of the Jebusite: the same is Jerusalem. The border went to the top of the mountain before the valley of Hinnom westward, at the end of the valley of the giants northward, then out by Kirjathjearim, Bethshemesh, and Ekron, and the west border was to the great sea. This is the coast of the children of Judah round about according to their families.

Unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh was given a part among the children of Judah according to the commandment of the Lord to Joshua: the city of Arba the father of Anak, which city is Hebron. And Caleb drove thence the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak. He went up thence to the inhabitants of Debir, whose name before was Kirjathsepher, and said, he that smiteth Kirjathsepher and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife. Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, took it, and got Achsah to wife. Achsah moved him to ask of her father a field, and said, give me a blessing, for thou hast given me a south land; give me also springs of water. And Caleb gave her the upper springs and the nether springs.

This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families, and the chapter counts out their cities district by district through verse 62: the uttermost cities toward the coast of Edom southward, twenty and nine cities with their villages; the cities in the valley in their groups of fourteen, sixteen, and nine; Ekron, Ashdod, and Gaza with their towns and villages unto the river of Egypt and the great sea; the cities in the mountains in their groups of eleven, nine, ten, six, and two; and six cities in the wilderness, all with their villages.

As for the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah could not drive them out, but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Judah at Jerusalem unto this day. Later on David conquered this place. The Jebusites thought David could not come in, that he was not getting past those walls, saying except thou take away the blind and the lame thou shalt not come in hither; nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion, the same is the city of David, and dwelt in the fort and built round about. The people that were left of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, whom Israel was not able utterly to destroy, upon those did Solomon levy a tribute of bondservice unto this day. They were forced to become our bondservants.

After the death of Joshua the children of Israel ask the Most High who shall go up first against the Canaanites, and the answer is Judah: behold, I have delivered the land into his hand. Judah asks Simeon his brother to come up with him into his lot, and promises to go likewise with Simeon into his lot, so Simeon went with him.

The Most High delivers the Canaanites and the Perizzites into Judah's hand, and they slay ten thousand men in Bezek. Adonibezek flees and is caught, and his thumbs and great toes are cut off. He confesses it himself: threescore and ten kings with their thumbs and great toes cut off gathered their meat under his table, and as he had done, so God requited him.

The children of Judah fought against Jerusalem, took it, smote it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire. This verse ties back into the history we just finished reading in Joshua. Judah was supposed to drive the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, out of the land, but could not, and the Jebusites dwelt with the children of Judah at Jerusalem. Jerusalem sat right on Judah's border by the valley of the son of Hinnom. The king of Jerusalem was already among the kings of the land which the children of Israel smote and whose land they possessed, so this fight in Judges is Judah taking the city itself.

Judah goes down against the Canaanites in the mountain, the south, and the valley, and against Hebron, which before was called Kirjath-arba, slaying Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. Caleb offers Achsah his daughter to wife to whoever smites Kirjath-sepher, and Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, takes it. Achsah asks her father for a blessing, springs of water with the south land, and Caleb gives her the upper springs and the nether springs. This is a review of the history we just read in Joshua; it was not that many days ago in the reading that we covered this, and it repeats again here at the opening of Judges.

The children of the Kenite, Moses' father in law, go up out of the city of palm trees with the children of Judah and dwell among the people in the wilderness of Judah. Judah goes with Simeon his brother, slays the Canaanites in Zephath and utterly destroys it, calling the city Hormah, and takes Gaza, Askelon, and Ekron with their coasts. The Most High was with Judah, and he drave out the inhabitants of the mountain, but could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron.

Hebron is given unto Caleb, as Moses said, and he expels thence the three sons of Anak. The children of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites that inhabited Jerusalem, but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem unto this day.

The house of Joseph goes up against Bethel, which before was called Luz, and the Most High was with them. The spies see a man come out of the city and promise him mercy for showing the entrance. They smite the city with the edge of the sword, but let the man and all his family go, and he goes into the land of the Hittites and builds a city and calls it Luz.

Tribe after tribe repeats the same failure: neither did Manasseh, nor Ephraim, nor Zebulun, nor Asher, nor Naphtali drive out the inhabitants of their cities, and the Amorites forced the children of Dan into the mountain. What we are reading is how we did not drive out all the inhabitants of the land, which the Most High had commanded us. Each tribe did not drive them out, and what did we do? We dwelt among them. When Israel was strong, we put the Canaanites to tribute, but we still did not utterly drive them out; we still dwelt among them. Chapter 2 gets into what that dwelling among the inhabitants of the land brought upon us.
